Construir figuras complicadas uniendo, c: Building complicated figures by joining, cutting and subtracting simple shapes has a name: constructive solid geometry. It was born in the 1960s and 1970s for computer-aided industrial design, and one of the first companies to use it for making images was MAGI, in New York, whose SynthaVision system described objects as combinations of spheres, cylinders and boxes. With it a good part of the computer sequences of Tron (1982) were made. Signed distances turned those operations into something as cheap as a min and a max, and that is why the technique has come back strongly in shaders.
